To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the F2-antigen is expressed on a subset of epithelial cells in a variety of human tissues, and that the expression is tissue and cell-type specific.

the epitope recognized by monoclonal antibody (mAb) F2, evocated against high M(r)-salivary mucins is the SO3- 3Gal beta 3GlcNAcc- moiety of the sulfo-Lewis a (Lea) antigen and that this epitope is found in a number of human and rat epithelial cells.
a monoclonal antibody, raised to human salivary mucin, recognizes the sulfo-Lewis (a) antigen in a number of human and rat mucin species and in a number of epithelial tissues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization and tissue distribution of a novel carbohydrate epitope on mucin glycoproteins.
the identification of the F2 epitope as a novel mucin epitope, and the characterization of the expression of the epitope in normal human and rat tissues.
the characterization of a novel monoclonal antibody, F2, which recognizes a high M(r) mucin epitope.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mAb F2 recognizes a carbohydrate determinant on a subset of epithelial cell glycoconjugates, which is not found on blood cells.

the mAb F2 is a useful tool for the detection of the SO3- 3Gal beta 2-3GlcNac moiety of sulfolactosylceramide in the extracellular matrix of epithelial cells, as well as the sulfo-Lea-antigen in epithelial cells of the salivary glands and the colon.

the F2-antigen is present on the apical surface of epithelial cells of the (sero) mucous secretory glands, the goblets of the colon, the suprabasally keratinized cells of the epidermis, the lining epithelial cells of cervical and esophagus glands and the epithelial cells of gastric intestinal metaplasia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the F2-antigen is a marker for the epithelial lineage, and may be used as an immunohistochemical marker in the differential diagnosis of tumors of epithelial origin.

the epitope of the mAb F2 is present in the SO3- 3Gal beta 3GlcNAcbeta1-R structure of the sulfo-Lewis a antigen, and that the F2- epitope is expressed in a number of epithelial cells in the human and rat.
the F2- epitope is expressed on epithelial cells of mucin-secreting glands and on the surface epithelia of skin and colon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mAb F2 can be used as a tool for the identification of cells that express the SO3- 3Gal beta 3GlcNAcbinding site in tissue sections.
we have developed a monoclonal antibody against a specific carbohydrate epitope on high molecular weight mucins that is expressed in a number of human epithelial cells.
the F2-antibody is a useful tool for histochemical studies of the expression of the sulfo-Lewis antigen.
